metadata.title: Accelerating Stochastic Gradient via Predictive Variance Reduction (Johnson & Zhang, 2013)
metadata.framework: variance-reduced stochastic gradient for finite-sum optimization
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:1403.4699.

nodes.name: Finite-sum optimization problem
nodes.statement: Minimize $P(w) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n f_i(w)$ where each $f_i : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ is the loss on the $i$-th training example. Assume each $f_i$ is smooth (Lipschitz-continuous gradient with constant $L$) and optionally $P$ is $\mu$-strongly convex.

nodes.name: SVRG gradient estimator
nodes.statement:
At the beginning of each epoch $s$, compute a full gradient snapshot $	ilde{\mu} = 
abla P(	ilde{w}) =  rac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n 
abla f_i(	ilde{w})$. During the epoch, for each step $t$ with randomly sampled index $i_t$, use the variance-reduced gradient estimator: $v_t = 
abla f_{i_t}(w_t) - 
abla f_{i_t}(	ilde{w}) + 	ilde{\mu}$. This estimator is unbiased ($\mathbb{E}[v_t] = 
abla P(w_t)$) and its variance approaches zero as $w_t 	o 	ilde{w} 	o w^*$.

nodes.name: SVRG algorithm
nodes.statement: SVRG alternates between: (1) Outer loop: compute full gradient $\tilde{\mu} = \nabla P(\tilde{w})$ and set $w_0 = \tilde{w}$. (2) Inner loop ($m$ steps): sample $i_t \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$, update $w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta v_t$. (3) Set $\tilde{w} = w_m$ (or average of $w_1, \ldots, w_m$) for the next epoch. The inner loop length $m$ is typically $O(n)$.

nodes.name: Linear convergence of SVRG
nodes.statement: If each $f_i$ is $L$-smooth and $P$ is $\mu$-strongly convex, SVRG with step size $\eta = 1/(10L)$ and inner loop length $m = \lceil 20L/\mu \rceil$ achieves linear convergence: $\mathbb{E}[P(\tilde{w}_s) - P(w^*)] \le \alpha^s [P(\tilde{w}_0) - P(w^*)]$ with $\alpha = 1/(10L/\mu) + 4/(20L/\mu - 1) < 1$. The per-epoch cost is $O(n + m)$ gradient evaluations, so the total complexity to reach $\epsilon$-accuracy is $O((n + L/\mu) \log(1/\epsilon))$.
conclusions: Matches or improves upon full gradient descent when $L/\mu \ll n$

nodes.name: Proof of linear convergence
nodes.statement: Key step: bound the variance of the SVRG estimator: $\mathbb{E}[\|v_t - \nabla P(w_t)\|^2] \le 4L [P(w_t) - P(w^*) + P(\tilde{w}) - P(w^*)]$ using smoothness. Combined with the descent lemma for SGD with bounded variance, this gives contraction per epoch.
nodes.proof_strategy: Bound variance of estimator using smoothness, then show epoch-level contraction.
